title: Make Beads Viewer decision-aware and canonical-actionable
description:
The static Viewer and raw robot planning do not understand the custom decision status: owner questions receive autonomous start wording, actionable counts differ from br ready, and status totals overlap. Make the checked export and operational view reflect the repository-owned decision workflow.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the workflow described above and observe the mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: This issue is an outcome container, not the preferred unit of execution. Its child leaves decompose discovery/design, implementation, negative/failure handling, integration, and proof so work can be reviewed and landed incrementally. External parent blockers remain authoritative; leaf tasks add the narrow prerequisite edges needed for safe parallel work. When every child is closed, a human or agent reopens this container, verifies the original description and structured acceptance criteria against combined evidence, records any residual gap as a new child, and closes the container only when no gap remains.
acceptance_criteria: Decision issues have a distinct visible status and owner queue; no decision receives autonomous claim or quick-win wording; the actionable count and identifiers equal br ready; active and blocked counts are disjoint and total correctly; graph, list, and detail remain visible; an automated export assertion prevents regression even if upstream bv still treats unknown statuses as open.
notes: Optional repository-tooling container; it improves visibility but does not gate constitutional product semantics beyond .4zy.
close_reason: Decision-aware Viewer projection and canonical-actionable regression guard are implemented and verified.

title: Enforce the cooperative owner-decision lifecycle and authoritative agent plan
description:
Repair the repository-owned Beads workflow guard. Beads Rust does not authenticate the project owner, so this is cooperative policy: active owner decisions must remain in the non-ready decision status, closed decisions retain provenance, reopening restores the decision workflow, normal work cannot silently enter it, and autonomous planning must use the checked repository wrapper rather than raw Viewer recommendations.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the workflow described above and observe the mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: The workflow container now has four explicit seams: transition evidence, validator enforcement, human/agent procedure, and the checked autonomous planning wrapper. It is a cooperative guard, not identity authentication. The wrapper is required before autonomous planning can be treated as authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: A transition-matrix fixture proves active decision labels and status agree, legitimate close passes and unblocks, reopen is restored to decision before autonomous use, claim or arbitrary status drift is detected, and ordinary work cannot carry decision status without both labels. The validator runs in repository-owned pre-commit and CI gates. br ready, scheduler, and .beads/agent-plan.sh expose no owner decision and agree on actionable IDs. Documentation states that actor metadata is not authentication and raw bv robot planning is advisory.
notes:
Future self: raw Viewer output is never an authority. The owner-decision workflow is cooperative: br actor metadata does not authenticate the project owner.

Authoritative operator commands:
- Owner queue: br --no-auto-import --no-auto-flush list --status decision --label decision-needed --label human-input --json; inspect .issues[]. A decision is active only with status=decision and both labels.
- Checked autonomous plan: ./.beads/agent-plan.sh. It reads br ready --json and br scheduler --json, validates them against .beads/issues.jsonl through .beads/validate-decisions.sh, emits stable candidate IDs and blocker reasons, and fails closed on missing, malformed, stale, or disagreeing evidence.
- Validation: ./.beads/validate-decisions.sh. Run it after every decision transition and before autonomous use.
- Raw Viewer: bv --db .beads --robot-plan is display/advisory output only. Never turn a raw Viewer recommendation into a claim.

Close/reopen procedure:
- After an explicit owner decision, close with br close <id> --reason <provenance> --transition-comment <context>. Then run the validator, owner queue query, and checked plan. Closed decisions retain both labels and close provenance.
- Reopen with br reopen <id> --reason <reason>, then immediately restore status and both labels with br update <id> --status decision --set-labels decision-needed --set-labels human-input. Run the validator and checked plan before any claim. Reopen, claim, label-only, or status drift is unsafe and must fail closed until restored.
- These commands record cooperative actor metadata only. They do not prove owner identity or authorize an agent to make an owner decision; owner direction remains required.
close_reason: All four cooperative owner-decision workflow children audited and proven

title: Implement the checked autonomous plan wrapper and Viewer quarantine
description:
Close the implementation gap between the cooperative Beads policy and the agent workflow. The current validator detects invalid decision state, but raw Viewer robot planning can still recommend a status=decision issue and documentation alone cannot prevent an autonomous agent from claiming it. Implement a small checked repository wrapper that fails closed, compares the canonical br ready/scheduler result with tracked issue status and labels, and refuses to consume untrusted raw Viewer planning. Keep actor metadata cooperative; do not claim owner authentication. Make the wrapper useful to both humans and agents and keep it independent of Omnirepo product authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Keep the wrapper small and fail-closed. It is a repository workflow adapter over br and tracked JSONL, not a replacement tracker or a Viewer fork. It must be deterministic under stale/missing data and produce evidence that the test suite can compare.
acceptance_criteria: A tracked wrapper is the only autonomous planning entry point. It derives candidates from br ready and the configured scheduler, validates status and decision labels against tracked JSONL, excludes every decision and deferred/container issue, emits stable issue IDs plus blocker/reason evidence, and exits nonzero on disagreement or stale data. Raw bv robot-plan is explicitly advisory and cannot be used for claims. Fixtures cover active, closed, reopened, relabeled, blocked, deferred, and normal work; CI and pre-commit run the wrapper and a decision can never reach a claimable recommendation.
notes: Future self: a false-positive actionable decision is a safety failure. Prefer refusing to plan over silently trusting a disagreement.
close_reason: Checked autonomous planner implemented and verified

title: Converge Omnirepo on its Constitution
description:
## Goal

Bring the current 0.8.x implementation into complete alignment with the ratified Omnirepo Constitution and routed Canon architecture.

## Current state

The quality baseline passes, but the product still exposes general repository creation, tag cloning, arbitrary shell execution, and ad hoc synchronization authority. It lacks canonical machine/source/repository configuration, source materialization, exact partials, contained atomic file transactions, verified scoped Git delivery, crash-recoverable durable accounting, bounded repair, and lawful release handling.

## Program rule

Decision-needed children are owner blockers and may not be guessed. Implementation preserves exact one-way authority, visible whole/section edges, independent outcomes, complete durable accounting, bounded sync-induced repair, and the constitutional limits. Actionable migration guidance is mandatory for breaking releases; an automated migrator is implemented only under its explicit decision.

## Success Criteria

See structured acceptance criteria; every mandatory child must close before the epic is eligible.
design: The delivery architecture is artifact-first and vertically sliced: owner decisions -> canonical machine authority -> immutable source snapshots/catalog -> explicit repository policy -> pure per-repository plans -> contained exact whole/partial transactions -> frozen repository/delta state -> configured verification -> operation-scoped local commit -> exact remote push -> one-repository initial pass -> bounded fleet fan-out -> separately invoked bounded repair -> durable final summary -> one public CLI. Legacy general orchestration is removed before replacement. Each outcome container is deferred while its leaf tasks are executed; after leaves close, reopen the container, verify its parent acceptance contract, and close it.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; the final implementation passes the Constitution gate across the full product surface; Cargo quality, MSRV, coverage, and pre-commit gates pass; public docs describe only the constitutional product.
notes: Autonomous agents claim leaf tasks from br ready or the repository agent-plan wrapper, never raw Viewer recommendations and never decision-status beads. Owner decisions close only from explicit owner answers and must update the smallest routed Canon page when they establish durable behavior. Optional P2 migration automation, resource limits, model-based testing, and ambient-adapter refactoring do not block the mandatory epic unless the owner explicitly promotes them.

UNAVAILABLE and intentionally absent effects are general repository orchestration, destination-to-source learning, semantic editing inside the sync engine, inference overriding present repository policy, agent repair without current-run causation, and destination deployment/dependency/release/secret/unrelated maintenance. The dependency graph follows durable artifact flow so later effects cannot manufacture missing authority. This serves Managed means authoritative; Precedence is declared, never guessed; The fleet advances despite stragglers; Humans and agents operate the same system.

title: Remove the arbitrary multi-repository run surface
description:
Boundary 1 forbids a general repository orchestrator. The public run command and src/run/runners.rs accept arbitrary shell strings and execute sh -c across repositories. Remove only this public and general runner surface, its tests, docs, verbose/global logging coupled to it, and any equivalent arbitrary fleet command. The repository-declared verifier is owned separately and must not be implemented here.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

design: This issue is an outcome container, not the preferred unit of execution. Its child leaves decompose discovery/design, implementation, negative/failure handling, integration, and proof so work can be reviewed and landed incrementally. External parent blockers remain authoritative; leaf tasks add the narrow prerequisite edges needed for safe parallel work. When every child is closed, a human or agent reopens this container, verifies the original description and structured acceptance criteria against combined evidence, records any residual gap as a new child, and closes the container only when no gap remains.

notes: Container for the three removal leaves. Claim children in order; after all close, reopen this container, verify its outcome contract, and close it.

title: Define source-repository materialization policy
description: OWNER DECISION — APPROVED 2026-08-13. Sources are local or remote Git repositories on main. A local source must be clean and on main; Omnirepo pins HEAD and never pulls or rewrites it. A remote source uses standard HTTPS or SSH with ordinary user credentials, lives beneath the machine-configured cache root, fetches latest main before every run, and creates an immutable pinned snapshot. Each fetch attempt times out after two minutes and may retry twice with bounded backoff. Offline or exhausted refresh fails rather than using stale authority. Missing, corrupt, wrong-remote, or unrecoverable cache state is discarded and cleanly cloned; explicit clean refresh is supported. Source hooks, filters, submodules, LFS, executable protocol helpers, and URL rewrites are disabled. An unavailable higher-priority source is never dropped or replaced by a lower source.
design: Decision protocol: (1) preserve all fixed constitutional and routed-Canon rules; (2) answer every valid, invalid, absent, ambiguous, failure, cancellation/restart, and compatibility case named in the description; (3) choose only among options inside Boundaries 1–5; (4) state exact precedence and authority tier; (5) record the active result on the smallest routed current-state Canon page and add or update stable validation paths; (6) close this bead only after the owner approves the complete matrix. Rationale: This choice changes canonical configuration, selection, CLI, or lifecycle behavior visible to users and agents. Canon forbids guessing missing policy, so implementation remains blocked until the owner supplies an explicit answer.
acceptance_criteria: Local clean-main sources pin HEAD without pull or mutation. Remote HTTPS/SSH sources refresh main into the configured cache, use one attempt plus at most two retries at two minutes each, publish only a complete immutable snapshot, and never use stale offline state. Recovery safely reclones only cache state. Interrupted staging is recoverable; concurrent materialization has one complete winner; credentials are redacted; dangerous Git mechanisms are disabled; unavailable higher authority remains a typed failure and never changes precedence.
notes: Owner selected fresh-main remote caches, clean pinned local sources, standard user Git authentication, fail-offline freshness, and bounded automatic cache recovery.
close_reason: Owner approved the complete decision contract; active guarantees are recorded in routed Canon.

comments.author: SilentFrog
comments.text:
## Decision: machine-owned bounded concurrency

Chosen schema for the canonical machine authority file at <HOME>/.omnirepo/config.yaml:

  concurrency:
    max_repositories: 4
    max_child_work: 8

- max_repositories: unsigned integer, domain 1..=32, default 4. It bounds active destination-repository lifecycles admitted by one fleet run.
- max_child_work: unsigned integer, domain 1..=64, default 8. It bounds the global machine-run permit pool for nested child work across active repositories.
- The mapping may be omitted. Either field may be omitted. Each omission uses its fixed default. A valid machine file remains required; field defaults do not turn a missing authority file into an implicit machine configuration.
- The limits are fixed values. No CPU-count, memory, environment, available-parallelism, or ambient Rayon inference is authoritative.
- The effective limits are frozen from one validated machine snapshot at run start. max_child_work is global across destinations, not a per-destination multiplier. Per-stage acquisition, per-repository serialization, and child resource classes belong to .17.2.

Validation matrix:

- Explicit zero is invalid for both fields. It never means unlimited, automatic, or disabled scheduling.
- Negative, fractional, string, boolean, sequence, mapping, null, out-of-range, or overflow values are invalid.
- Unknown or duplicate fields are errors under the existing strict YAML policy. Top-level max_repositories or max_child_work and the same fields in source or destination configuration are unknown fields, not alternate authorities.
- Invalid machine configuration fails shared configuration preflight before synchronization effects.
- No config path override is added. The fixed machine path from .18 remains authoritative.

CLI contract:

- Only sync accepts transient --max-repositories N and --max-child-work N caps. Each value is a positive integer no greater than the corresponding validated machine value. A supplied value can only lower that run cap; omission uses the machine value. Values above the machine cap, zero, negative, malformed, or out of range are invocation errors.
- The overrides are not persisted, do not alter the machine file, and cannot be supplied by destination or source policy. setup and validate do not accept scheduler overrides.
- Invalid command-line values fail before a fleet run is created. A valid sync with invalid machine configuration follows the shared configuration failure and run-record rules from .27.
- No CLI option changes fleet membership, source order, source priority, repository applicability, repository commands, or repair-agent priority.

Scheduling boundary:

The machine scheduler owns repository admission and the global child-work budget. A destination policy may select applicable managed content and declare verification commands, but it cannot raise, lower, or replace either machine cap. Queue and completion order affect performance only; they cannot affect source precedence, membership, or final accounting. Implementation must use explicit bounded permits and must not inherit an ambient Rayon pool as a hidden authority.

Constitutional decision:

Options considered: 3 | Pruned at boundary: 1

- Effect: record this schema and matrix in the Bead — AVAILABLE.
- Effect: clarify machine concurrency ownership in the routed configuration-authority page — AVAILABLE.
- Effect: let destination policy redefine fleet-wide concurrency or source priority — UNAVAILABLE. The Constitution says: “Machine configuration alone governs fleet membership, authoritative sources, and source priority” and rejects “destination configuration that redefines fleet-wide authority.” Tension pair 2 also says repository-local controls must never let a destination redefine authoritative sources or their priority.
- Discarded destination-owned fleet scheduling because it crosses that authority boundary.
- Fixed machine limits with lower-only transient CLI caps rank above no CLI override because they preserve visible machine authority while giving an operator a bounded per-run reduction. They serve “Shared synchronization authority must have visible edges” and “Parallel speed over deterministic completion order—but never at the cost of configured verification or complete accounting of every repository's outcome.”
- Ambient or zero-as-unbounded scheduling was not chosen. It would hide the bound and undermine the same configured-verification and complete-accounting limit.
- No numeric default or range is prescribed by the Constitution. This is constitutional silence; owner delegation makes the fixed conservative engineering choice available.

Chosen: two explicit machine fields, fixed defaults 4 and 8, finite domains 1..=32 and 1..=64, and sync-only lower-bound CLI caps.

Serves: Managed means authoritative; Convention governs until intent is declared; Shared synchronization authority must have visible edges; The fleet advances despite stragglers; Precedence is declared, never guessed.
Strains: none.
Silence: the Constitution sets no numeric defaults, ranges, or CLI override syntax; those values are engineering choices within the owner delegation.

Evidence: Canon architecture/configuration-authority.md now records machine ownership, schema, defaults, invalid and zero behavior, lower-only overrides, and the no-destination-authority edge. No implementation code was changed.

Canon impact: updated — machine concurrency fields and their authority, validation, and bounded CLI override invariants are now durable.

title: Specify nested repository and child-work scheduling semantics
description:
Define how repository slots interact with verification, Git, source acquisition, and agent child processes, including fairness, cancellation, backpressure, and per-repository serialization.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: A single numeric limit is insufficient when one repository can spawn multiple bounded child effects.
acceptance_criteria: The design identifies every token/resource class, acquisition order, no-deadlock rule, cancellation release, and observability event; no ambient Rayon pool remains authoritative.
notes: Implementation belongs to .47; this task produces its contract.
close_reason: Nested scheduling contract, Canon clarification, handoffs, and verification complete

comments.author: SilentFrog
comments.text:
## Decision: nested bounded scheduling contract

Inputs and scope

This contract consumes the machine snapshot from omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.17.1: max_repositories is the global destination slot limit and max_child_work is the global child-work permit limit. The scheduler freezes both effective values once for a run. CLI lower caps are already resolved before this contract. This Bead defines scheduling only; source authority, repository scope, verification policy, timeouts, leases, journal schema, and repair eligibility remain owned by their existing contracts.

Resource and token classes

1. Repository slot: one machine-wide permit for one admitted destination-repository lifecycle. A slot is held from lease-ready admission through one terminal initial-pass or repair outcome. Initial pass and the later separate repair operation reacquire slots; they do not overlap. At most max_repositories slots are live.
2. Source work: one operation per source ID at a time. Needed source snapshots are deduplicated. A source fetch, clone, or other external materialization uses one child-work permit but no destination slot. A repository whose required source is pending stays queued without a slot; a source failure gives dependent work a typed source failure and never promotes a lower-priority source.
3. Verification work: one child-work permit per configured check process. Checks run one at a time per repository in declared order, and every configured check is attempted even after an earlier failure. The repository stage gate remains held between checks.
4. Git work: one child-work permit per Git operation. A destination repository has at most one Git operation at a time and cannot overlap Git with synchronization, verification, or agent work. Source Git belongs to the source-work kind.
5. Agent work: one child-work permit per repair-agent invocation. At most one agent invocation is active for a repository. The agent receives only the bounded repair input already defined by the lifecycle contract; initial fleet work never invokes an agent.
6. Child pool: all source, verification, Git, and agent operations draw from one global max_child_work pool. Kind labels and the per-source/per-repository stage gates are the only per-kind limits; no new per-kind configuration authority is introduced. A top-level child operation owns one permit for its complete process tree. Contained descendants do not acquire nested scheduler permits; their process-tree count is reported as documented fixed overhead and is terminated with the parent.

Per-repository lifecycle and phase boundaries

A canonical destination repository has one stage gate and one lease. It cannot overlap synchronization, any configured check, Git mutation or publication, repair-agent contact, or repair reapplication. The initial fleet pass runs independently for each admitted repository. After the initial pass barrier, a separate repair queue may process eligible failures with the same slot and child pools. A failure, timeout, or hang in one repository releases only that repository resources after cleanup and does not cancel valid peers. A busy lease consumes no repository slot; the busy outcome is recorded and peers continue.

Fixed acquisition order and no-deadlock rule

Every admission or child transition follows this order: (1) observe cancellation and journal-writer health; (2) establish source readiness for source-dependent work or acquire the canonical repository lease; (3) acquire the repository slot when destination work is admitted; (4) persist and acknowledge the stage intent; (5) acquire exactly one child-work permit; (6) start the contained child process tree; (7) capture the typed result; (8) terminate and reap the complete tree; (9) release the child permit; and (10) persist the result and advance or terminalize the stage. No permit is held while waiting for a repository slot, lease, journal intent, or another permit. No child operation acquires a second permit. A repository slot and stage gate are not released until its lifecycle state is terminal or the durable cancellation/recovery contract has recorded the in-flight state. This order prevents lock-order deadlock and makes durable intent precede every external effect.

Fairness and backpressure

Source and child requests use one bounded FIFO ticket queue. A source or repository has at most one pending request; a repository that completes one child operation is requeued at the tail, so a long check list cannot monopolize permits. Tickets use frozen canonical plan order for ties. Queue order affects performance only and never source precedence, membership, or final outcomes. A ready peer can advance while another peer is slow, failed, or waiting for a child timeout, within the configured limits.

The scheduler stores one compact state record per selected repository and source and does not expand every future check or agent attempt into an unbounded queue. Before admission or a new external effect, the journal writer must accept the required intent. Journal saturation pauses new admission and new effects, while active operations finish only when their intent/result can still be accounted. Writer failure stops new effects, emits typed scheduler or cancellation events, and terminalizes affected queued or active work under the journal contract. No event or repository outcome is dropped, and workers never write terminal output directly.

Cancellation and release

Cancellation stops new source, repository, and child admission, closes child input, requests complete process-tree termination, and force-terminates after five seconds; a repeated cancellation may force immediately. Queued repositories receive typed not-started cancellation outcomes. Running children release their child permit only after every descendant terminates and is reaped. The repository slot, stage gate, and lease release only after the repository cancellation or failure state is journaled or durable recovery records the in-flight state. Completed synchronization, commit, or push effects are reconciled and retained, never rolled back. Cancellation and writer failure still produce one terminal outcome for every selected repository when the journal remains writable.

Observability

The frozen run snapshot records configured and effective repository and child limits. Scheduler events are durable through the single writer and include run ID, repository or source ID, stage, resource kind, ticket, active counts, queue depth, high-water marks, permit acquisition and release, lease-busy, journal backpressure or failure, cancellation, child result, and terminal outcome. Event checkpoints are monotonic. The run summary includes queued, admitted, running, cancelled, failed, and successful repository counts plus resource high-water marks. Routine success remains quiet; workers do not print shared terminal chatter.

Implementation handoff with exact Bead links

- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47 owns the bounded fleet and child-work scheduler. It must preserve sequential per-repository stages, complete accounting, no oversubscription, and unspecified completion order.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47.1 implements repository admission queues and permits. It must stop admission on cancellation or journal-writer failure and keep active count at or below max_repositories.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47.2 implements the global/per-kind child permits, fixed acquisition order, and per-repository serialization. It must release only after descendant termination and prove no deadlock.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47.3 integrates bounded journal backpressure and typed writer-failure scheduling events without dropping outcomes.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47.4 proves FIFO fairness and peer progress with mixed fast, slow, failed, and hung repositories; it must not create a completion-order guarantee.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.47.5 tests saturation, nested races, cancellation, process leaks, queue bounds, permit return, and every-repository accounting with barriers and a fake clock.
- omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.64.3 owns the concurrent-producer/single-writer queue and its exact backpressure and acknowledgement contract; omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.39 owns leases, cancellation, recovery, and stale-owner proof; omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.10 and omni-constitutional-convergence-2r9.69.3 consume this contract for the initial pass and never invoke repair agents.

No ambient authority

The scheduler must use explicit permit accounting and explicit workers. A global Rayon pool, par_iter, CPU-count autodetection, RAYON_NUM_THREADS, or any environment-derived worker count is not authoritative. Coordinator and single-writer control tasks are fixed overhead only; they never run destination effects or bypass the configured permits.

Constitutional decision

Options considered: 3 | Pruned at boundary: 1

- Record this self-contained scheduling contract in the Bead — AVAILABLE.
- Update the routed fleet-lifecycle page with the durable bounded-scheduling invariants — AVAILABLE.
- Use only a repository slot and let each repository create unbounded source/check/Git/agent children — UNAVAILABLE as a direction that crosses the Constitution tension: “Parallel speed over deterministic completion order—but never at the cost of configured verification or complete accounting of every repository's outcome.” It also strains Principle 5, which rejects sacrificing broad progress for a straggler.
- Let destination policy choose its own fleet slots or child limits — DISCARDED because Principle 2 says “Machine configuration alone governs fleet membership, authoritative sources, and source priority” and rejects “destination configuration that redefines fleet-wide authority.” The contract therefore keeps all scheduler permits machine-run and visible.
- A global child pool with fixed per-source/per-repository gates, FIFO requeue, journal-aware admission, and post-reap release ranks above separate uncoordinated pools. It serves “The fleet advances despite stragglers,” “Shared synchronization authority must have visible edges,” and the tension pair requiring configured verification and complete accounting. It also preserves the lifecycle boundary: “Never become a general repository orchestrator.”
- No completion-order promise, throughput target, or queue implementation library is added. The Constitution is silent on those mechanisms; engineering chooses the simplest bounded contract.

Chosen: one machine-wide repository-slot pool, one machine-wide child-work pool with explicit kind gates, fixed acquisition order, bounded FIFO fairness, journal-aware backpressure, post-reap release, and durable scheduler events.

Serves: The fleet advances despite stragglers; Shared synchronization authority must have visible edges; Parallel speed over deterministic completion order—but never at the cost of configured verification or complete accounting.
Strains: none.
Silence: the Constitution does not prescribe FIFO, queue representation, permit kind names, or process-tree token accounting; these are implementation-facing choices within the fixed authority and lifecycle boundaries.

Evidence: No scheduler code was changed. The full contract is recorded here; the routed Canon fleet-lifecycle page records the durable summary.

This ordering removes any contradiction around writer backpressure: no repository or child permit is held while waiting for journal intent or a slot. A busy lease terminalizes the already-accounted request without consuming a repository slot. The stage gate remains held through the lifecycle, but no second child permit is acquired.

title: Define configuration serialization, discovery, and conflict policy
description: OWNER DECISION — APPROVED 2026-08-13. YAML is the only canonical configuration serialization. Fixed locations are ~/.omnirepo/config.yaml for machine authority, destination-root .omnirepo.yaml for repository policy, and source-root .omnirepo/source.yaml for source declarations. Discovery checks only these exact files. Unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys, unreadable/non-regular candidates, malformed YAML, aliases that resolve to another authority identity, and any competing or legacy config at the same authority tier are explicit errors; they never become absence or fallback. Arbitrary CLI config substitution is unavailable. Paths follow the approved portable UTF-8 representation.
design: Decision protocol: (1) preserve all fixed constitutional and routed-Canon rules; (2) answer every valid, invalid, absent, ambiguous, failure, cancellation/restart, and compatibility case named in the description; (3) choose only among options inside Boundaries 1–5; (4) state exact precedence and authority tier; (5) record the active result on the smallest routed current-state Canon page and add or update stable validation paths; (6) close this bead only after the owner approves the complete matrix. Rationale: This choice changes canonical configuration, selection, CLI, or lifecycle behavior visible to users and agents. Canon forbids guessing missing policy, so implementation remains blocked until the owner supplies an explicit answer.
acceptance_criteria: Only the three fixed YAML paths load. Strict schemas reject unknown fields, duplicate keys, malformed/unreadable/non-regular/aliased candidates, competing formats, legacy .omni.yaml authority, and arbitrary CLI config overrides. True destination-policy absence remains distinguishable from every present-invalid state. Round-trip and negative fixtures pass.
notes: Owner selected YAML only and clear tiered paths. Legacy or competing config produces an actionable error; no compatibility fallback is retained.

title: Define managed-item identity, precedence, and collision semantics
description: OWNER DECISION — APPROVED 2026-08-13. Every managed item has an explicit stable ID using ASCII lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens. IDs are exact and case-sensitive. Duplicate IDs within one source fail. Across ordered sources, declarations with the same ID or declarations targeting the same compatible managed boundary are resolved only by configured source priority; completion order and content never affect the winner. Whole-file versus section collisions, overlapping/differently named sections that cannot coexist unambiguously, collisions within the same source, and attempts to manage protected authority files fail before destination mutation. title: Retire general-purpose repository creation
description:
## Constitutional finding

Growth Directive 5 says to grow through file and section synchronization, "not by expanding into general repository orchestration." Boundary 1 limits Omnirepo to synchronization plus commit, push, checks, and sync-induced repair.

## Current evidence

src/bin/main.rs exposes new; src/new/project_creation.rs creates arbitrary repositories, copies tag-selected templates, and runs git init. README.md presents repository creation as a core product feature.

## Scope

Remove the general new command and its production module, tests, and documentation. Any future onboarding must be a synchronization-specific setup path driven by the constitutional configuration and inference model, not a generic project generator.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the current public surface or workflow described above and observe the stated boundary or gate failure.
design: This issue is an outcome container, not the preferred unit of execution. Its child leaves decompose discovery/design, implementation, negative/failure handling, integration, and proof so work can be reviewed and landed incrementally. External parent blockers remain authoritative; leaf tasks add the narrow prerequisite edges needed for safe parallel work. When every child is closed, a human or agent reopens this container, verifies the original description and structured acceptance criteria against combined evidence, records any residual gap as a new child, and closes the container only when no gap remains.
acceptance_criteria: The public CLI has no general new command; project creation/template-generation code and obsolete tests are removed; README and package wording no longer claim general project generation; installation-to-first-sync onboarding remains covered by the configuration/inference beads; all Canon quality gates pass.
notes: Outcome container. Children separate inventory, deletion, and enduring negative proof so future setup work cannot silently revive scaffolding.
close_reason: CONTAINER ROLLUP closed: every descendant leaf is closed with evidence (see the leaf comments). The original container acceptance criteria were verified against the combined leaf evidence; no residual gap remains. This container was left in_progress after its leaves closed; the rollup closes it and unblocks the dependent containers.

title: Define managed-text encoding and exactness contract
description: OWNER DECISION — APPROVED 2026-08-13. Managed content is an opaque byte sequence. Omnirepo acquires, compares, stores, and writes whole-file and managed-section payloads byte-for-byte. It does not decode, normalize, transcode, repair, or reject content because it is invalid UTF-8. BOMs, Unicode encodings, invalid byte sequences, LF/CRLF/mixed line endings, and final-newline presence are authoritative bytes. Text decoding is allowed only for the delimiter lines needed to locate a partial section under the delimiter contract; failure to recognize unambiguous delimiter lines fails the partial operation without mutation.
design: Decision protocol: (1) preserve all fixed constitutional and routed-Canon rules; (2) answer every valid, invalid, absent, ambiguous, failure, cancellation/restart, and compatibility case named in the description; (3) choose only among options inside Boundaries 1–5; (4) state exact precedence and authority tier; (5) record the active result on the smallest routed current-state Canon page and add or update stable validation paths; (6) close this bead only after the owner approves the complete matrix. Rationale: This choice fixes externally observable exact-text, delimiter, or replacement behavior. The Constitution selects authority and hard boundaries but intentionally does not choose encoding syntax, metadata, or durability mechanics; engineering must not manufacture those values.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog, whole-file, and partial-section paths preserve every authoritative byte exactly. Byte equality is the no-op criterion. BOM, invalid UTF-8, Unicode, LF, CRLF, mixed line endings, and final-newline fixtures pass without normalization. Partial delimiter recognition never changes payload bytes and ambiguity/recognition failure leaves the file unchanged.
notes: Owner selected exact bytes, not UTF-8-only or decoded Unicode. This directly replaces the legacy String/Response::text model.

title: Push only the recorded OID to the selected ref
description:
Perform a bounded noninteractive push of the exact recorded commit/ref under sanitized environment and credentials, journaling intent before contact and response evidence after.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Ordinary git push of a branch can incidentally publish pre-existing commits, tags, or newer HEAD.
acceptance_criteria: Transport offers only selected ref/OID; no tag/other branch/incidental ref is sent; timeout/cancel terminates children; credentials/output are redacted; remote rejection is typed.
notes: Deployment or release effects are unavailable.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: push only the recorded OID to the selected ref (src/lifecycle/remote_push.rs, tests in remote_push_tests.rs, 2 focused tests on Rust 1.86). The transport offers exactly one refspec, `<recorded-oid>:<selected ref>`, with --no-tags and --porcelain, so no tag, other branch, or incidental ref is ever sent (verified: the bare upstream carries exactly refs/heads/main after the push). The repository intent (Operation::Push) is journaled before contact; response evidence (stage push) is journaled after. The child runs in its own process group under a hard deadline; a timeout or cancellation terminates the child and its descendants, and output is bounded and sanitized to inert text. A remote rejection is a typed failure (non-fast-forward proven with a real divergent upstream). Credentials cannot leak: the frozen transport is already credential-free and the askpass helpers are neutralized. title: Reconcile accepted-but-disconnected, timeout, crash, and retry ambiguity
description:
Query the exact remote ref under policy after uncertain outcomes and compare it to recorded expected old/new OIDs before deciding success, retry, conflict, or failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Blind retry can duplicate effects or overwrite unrelated remote movement.
acceptance_criteria: Remote=new records success without repush; remote=old may retry within policy; any third OID fails without force; crash/restart never publishes a different commit or ref.
notes: Journal all observations and decisions.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: reconcile accepted-but-disconnected, timeout, crash, and retry ambiguity (src/lifecycle/push_reconcile.rs, tests in push_reconcile_tests.rs, 3 focused tests on Rust 1.86). After a bounded push attempt the exact remote ref is re-read with a hardened, noninteractive ls-remote of only the selected reference: a remote that already carries the recorded OID records success without repush (the accepted-but-disconnected case); a remote still carrying the pre-push OID allows a retry within policy (the timeout/crash case — the push never landed); any third OID is a typed conflict that fails without force. A missing remote ref is a retry-allowed state. Crash/restart can never publish a different commit or ref: the refspec is always the recorded OID against the frozen target. Rust 1.86: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 1028 workspace tests, doc, build, pre-commit green. Autoreview clean (TruffleHog clean, 0.99). No Canon impact.

comments.author: RoseHare
comments.text:
Coverage inventory (2026-08-13, RoseHare; read-only inspection; no thresholds changed)

Normative contract
- canon/standards.md: coverage spans the workspace, all targets, and all features with locked dependencies. Floors are at least 95% lines, 80% functions, and 80% regions. A threshold failure remains a failed check; report generation may continue and retain diagnostics, but it must not mask the gate.
- Cargo.toml sets rust-version = 1.86. There is no rust-toolchain.toml or rust-toolchain file, so aliases do not pin a toolchain themselves.

Coverage command paths
1. Local Cargo aliases in .cargo/config.toml:7-8:
   - coverage = llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked --summary-only --fail-under-lines 95 --fail-under-functions 80 --fail-under-regions 80. This is the only local alias that directly gates all three floors.
   - coverage-html = llvm-cov --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked --html --output-dir coverage. It generates HTML only and has no fail-under flags.
2. CI .github/workflows/coverage.yml is the only workflow containing llvm-cov/coverage commands. It triggers on pull_request, pushes to main/staging/trying, and workflow_dispatch. It installs floating stable Rust with llvm-tools-preview, caches Rust artifacts, then installs prebuilt cargo-llvm-cov@0.8.7 through taiki-e/install-action@v2.85.11 with fallback: none.
3. CI report sequence: mkdir -p coverage; cargo llvm-cov clean --workspace; one test/instrumentation run with --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked --no-report; summary report with --fail-under-lines 95, --fail-under-functions 80, --fail-under-regions 80 piped to tee coverage/summary.txt; LCOV to coverage/lcov.info; HTML to coverage/; exit with captured threshold status. Upload runs if: always(), uploads coverage/ as coverage-reports, errors if no files, retention 14 days.
4. README.md:67-109 duplicates the aliases, a standalone LCOV command, and a full summary/LCOV/HTML sequence. Local setup is manual: Rust 1.86.0 plus rustfmt/clippy; Rust 1.87.0 to build cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7 from source; llvm-tools-preview on Rust 1.86. The README says the full sequence is the same as CI, but its snippet omits CI set +e, PIPESTATUS capture, set -e, and final exit.
5. pr-lint-test.yml and create-release.yml run normal tests/builds but no coverage. pre-commit has no coverage command. No other llvm-cov references were found outside the paths above.

Artifacts and retention
- CI/local outputs are coverage/summary.txt (text summary), coverage/lcov.info (LCOV), and coverage/html/... (HTML plus per-source pages). .gitignore ignores coverage/ and *.lcov; target/ is also ignored, including target/llvm-cov-target profraw data. No coverage output is tracked in Git.
- Existing ignored local artifacts are not authoritative: summary.txt totals 96.08% lines, 84.76% functions, 84.64% regions (passes current floors); coverage/html/index.html is newer than the nested coverage/html/html/index.html, whose totals differ (96.33/87.38/85.16) and timestamp is 14:19 versus 14:42. The nested/stale tree demonstrates that local output directories can retain duplicate reports. CI starts from a fresh checkout but the workflow does not remove coverage/ before writing.

Threshold/installation masking risks
- CI threshold propagation is correct for the cargo report status: set +e permits the failing threshold report to continue, PIPESTATUS[0] saves cargo llvm-cov status rather than tee status, set -e is restored, reports are generated, and exit coverage_status preserves the failure. Artifact upload always runs for diagnostics.
- The README full-report sequence is not a gate. A threshold failure in the pipeline can be replaced by tee status (or followed by successful LCOV/HTML commands) because the snippet has no explicit status capture/final exit and does not require a shell with errexit/pipefail. Only the standalone coverage alias has direct gate propagation; coverage-html and standalone LCOV are diagnostic-only.
- CI captures only PIPESTATUS[0]. A tee/write failure is not incorporated, so a failed or partial summary write can be treated as a passing threshold if later report generation still succeeds. The downstream report and upload steps may catch common filesystem failures, but this status is not explicit.
- Local aliases are not pinned to Rust 1.86. CI coverage uses floating stable, while the normative minimum is 1.86; compiler/LLVM drift can change measured totals. The local docs and CI therefore have different toolchain selection.
- Coverage is not installed by the normal build instructions. It needs cargo-llvm-cov plus llvm-tools-preview for the measured toolchain. In this workspace, cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.7 is present but rustup and llvm-tools-preview are unavailable; cargo coverage exits 1 with “failed to find llvm-tools-preview”, so no fresh local measurement was possible.

Checks/evidence
- cargo fmt --all -- --check: exit 0.
- git diff --check: exit 0.
- cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1: exit 0.
- cargo coverage probe: expected exit 1 because the local llvm-tools-preview component is missing; this confirms the installation assumption, not a source/test failure.
- constitution_scan.py confirms CONSTITUTION.md and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md wiring; working-tree diff is only the Bead JSONL mutation. No repository files were edited.

Constitution gate: PASS (4 effects inspected, coverage: full relevant local command/config/artifact paths and process traces; CI runner/network transient execution was unavailable locally and is stated as a limit). description:

title: Define repository synchronization transaction and failure residue
description: OWNER DECISION — APPROVED 2026-08-13. All managed operations targeting one destination file form one atomic group. Groups are preflighted and attempted in deterministic order; a failed group does not stop independent groups in the same repository. Successful authoritative group writes remain when another group, verification, commit, or push fails; there is no repository-wide rollback. Verification failure leaves authorized sync writes but no Omnirepo commit. Every failed repair attempt removes its agent-created delta back to the attempt baseline while retaining authoritative sync writes. Commit failure leaves authorized worktree changes with the pre-existing index exact; push failure may leave the exact local operation commit. Forbidden, concurrent, or late verifier/agent residue is restored and never enters Git. Crash/cancel residue follows journal recovery.

title: Implement bounded concurrent producer to single-writer journal flow
description:
Accept events from fleet workers through one ordered writer, acknowledge required checkpoints, enforce owner-decided backpressure, and propagate writer failure to admission/cancellation logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Parallel workers must not corrupt or reorder the durable record, and slow persistence cannot silently lose outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Required checkpoints are monotonic and acknowledged before their effects; concurrent producers lose none; backpressure is bounded; writer failure stops new effects per policy and is visible to every affected repository.
notes: Scheduler integration is .47/.39.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: bounded concurrent-producer to single-writer journal flow (src/lifecycle/journal.rs, tests in src/lifecycle/journal/journal_tests.rs, 7 focused tests on Rust 1.86). One writer thread owns the run-record file; producers submit typed events through a bounded std::sync_channel (default capacity 64, configurable) with blocking send (bounded backpressure) and non-blocking try_submit returning Full. The writer owns checkpoint allocation (producer claims ignored, assigned strictly monotonic 1..n, acknowledged only after the exact JSONL line is appended and fsync'd when sync_each_append is set) — ack-before-effects contract. Transition validation runs in the writer, so concurrent producers cannot corrupt run/repository state; validation rejections fail the submit without poisoning, persistence failures (write/sync) poison the journal so every later submit fails and no new effect can be acknowledged. Shutdown drains, syncs the tail, and joins. Concurrent test: 6 producers x 20 events, 120 unique monotonic acks, no loss, record contains intent plus every event. Writer-owned checkpoints proven against producer-claimed values. Rust 1.86: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 786 workspace tests, doc, build, pre-commit green. Autoreview clean (TruffleHog clean, 0.94). title: Implement replay, truncated-tail handling, and incomplete-run discovery
description:
Read schema-valid records, distinguish complete from interrupted/corrupt/unsupported tails, reconstruct last durable state, and expose incomplete runs for coordinator recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: A crash must not turn partial bytes into success or discard evidence already durable.
acceptance_criteria: Valid prefix plus truncated tail replays exactly under policy; corruption and version errors are typed; startup discovers incomplete records without scanning unrelated files; replay is deterministic and side-effect free.
notes: Operational resume/terminalize choices belong to .38/.39.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: deterministic side-effect-free journal replay and incomplete-run discovery (src/lifecycle/replay.rs, tests in src/lifecycle/replay/replay_tests.rs, 8 focused tests on Rust 1.86). Replay reads one record once (bounded at 64 MiB, regular-file check), parses every line against the canonical event schema, validates transitions through the shared EventLog, and classifies the tail: Clean (valid terminal run), Truncated (final chunk without terminating newline — the writer was interrupted mid-line, never parsed, never authoritative), Corrupt (complete line with typed parse/transition reason), or UnsupportedVersion (typed with the version). title: Build repository-owned test evidence system
description:
Create the mandatory test-and-evidence layer for the whole convergence program. This workstream composes the low-level hermetic fixtures from .9 into one repository-owned test taxonomy, structured event/evidence format, replay tooling, coverage attribution, clean-HOME public-binary runner, executable acceptance journey matrix, failure-preserving orchestration, and test isolation checks. It does not duplicate product implementations, .9 fixture mechanics, .46 hostile-case ownership, .48 platform execution, .49 scale measurements, or .62 optional model-based testing. It gives every required behavior one primary test owner while preserving deliberate supporting views.

The suite must preserve the full feature set: canonical machine and source authority, optional destination policy and inference, exact whole files and bounded partial sections, containment, independent fleet progress, verification, scoped Git delivery, durable records, crash recovery, bounded repair, optional delegated migration, setup, packaging, and human/agent parity. It must prove forbidden legacy, reverse-authority, semantic-sync, outside-root, unbounded-repair, and hidden-agent-only paths are absent. Use the hermetic harness and owner decisions; do not invent limits, formats, or policy in test code.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every constitutional product component has an explicit primary unit/component/E2E owner in .74.1; clean-environment scripts exercise human and agent entry points; each test step emits structured, redacted, replayable evidence with stable run, repository, stage, and seed identities; failures preserve logs and exit status; coverage and required quality gates remain authoritative; no test depends on ambient HOME, credentials, network, installed agents, wall-clock sleeps, or a production-only hidden path. Child ownership is non-overlapping: .74.1 routes, .74.2 unit fixtures, .74.3 public E2E runner, .74.4 evidence, .74.5 replay, .74.6 coverage ownership, .74.7 executable journeys, .74.8 aggregate execution, and .74.9 suite-level isolation.
design: This is a mandatory test-system outcome container. Children deliberately separate test taxonomy, unit fixtures, black-box scripts, structured evidence, replay, coverage, journey matrices, and execution hygiene. Product policy stays in product beads and owner decisions; test code may only assert selected behavior. A child can run in parallel when its dependency artifacts are ready, but the final acceptance suite cannot close until every required evidence path is present.
acceptance_criteria: Every constitutional product component has an explicit unit, component, or end-to-end test owner; clean-environment scripts exercise human and agent entry points; each test step emits structured, redacted, replayable evidence with stable run, repository, stage, and seed identities; failures preserve logs and exit status; coverage and required quality gates remain authoritative; no test depends on ambient HOME, credentials, network, installed agents, wall-clock sleeps, or a production-only hidden path.
notes: Mandatory test-system container and integration point. .9 is the low-level fixture layer; .74 is the test-system composition layer; .74.7 is the sole executable final-journey owner; .74.1 is the sole primary ownership and traceability matrix. Keep specialized adversarial, platform, scale, and model suites in their own workstreams and register them in .74.1.

title: Define the canonical test taxonomy and constitutional traceability matrix
description:
Define one canonical test-routing and traceability matrix for the entire product. It is the authoritative index for required behavior, not a second implementation and not a place to choose owner policy. Classify every required behavior as unit, component/adapter, black-box E2E, adversarial, platform, scale, or optional hardening; map each production module, public command, constitutional principle/boundary/tension limit, owner decision, and failure stage to exactly one primary test owner plus deliberate supporting views. The matrix must include fixture identity, expected positive or negative effect, stable case ID, structured evidence identity, and downstream acceptance bead. The constitutional view and adversarial view are projections of this matrix, not competing ownership systems. Mark constitutional silence and optional methods explicitly instead of filling gaps with test assumptions.

## Acceptance Criteria

A checked-in matrix has no unowned required behavior, no duplicate primary owner, no stale/orphan reference, and no test that silently selects policy. It contains the complete clause-to-effect mapping required by the final gate, including every Boundary 1-5 prohibition, every never-at-the-cost-of limit, managed whole/partial ownership, authority direction, fleet progress, human/agent parity, release guidance, and all failure stages. It names the primary implementation/test bead, supporting adversarial/platform/scale views, expected artifacts, and replay identity for every row. A validator fails on duplicate ownership, missing required rows, stale issue IDs, or a decision value embedded in test data. The final acceptance suite and hostile matrix consume this index rather than reimplementing a second map.
design: This is the single routing layer for test ownership. The previous constitutional and adversarial matrices become maintained projections under this canonical matrix: they may add view-specific assertions but cannot claim a second primary owner. Keep product policy in owner-decision beads and routed Canon; tests only assert the selected value. This consolidation removes overlap while preserving full clause coverage and hostile negative testing.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in canonical matrix maps every required behavior and constitutional clause to one primary test owner, supporting views, fixture, expected effect, negative case where applicable, evidence identity, and downstream acceptance bead; constitutional and adversarial projections are generated or validated from it; stale, orphaned, duplicate, policy-selecting, or missing rows fail validation.
notes: Canonical owner for test taxonomy and traceability. .32.1 and .46.5 are merged into this ownership model; their distinct constitutional and adversarial coverage remains as views and acceptance rows, not duplicate matrices. Future implementation beads must link to a matrix row before closure.

title: Build deterministic unit-test fixtures and domain suites
description:
Build reusable deterministic unit-test fixtures and cross-cutting domain contract suites for typed machine configuration, source catalogs, repository-policy presence, selectors, precedence, plans, whole/partial content, path identities, state snapshots, authorized deltas, journal events, process outcomes, repair eligibility, CLI statuses, and release identities. This bead owns shared fixture types and contracts that span components; module-specific behavior tests remain with their implementation child leaves and are registered in .74.1. Keep pure tests independent of real HOME, network, Git, clocks, processes, and terminal output; use table-driven cases for valid, absent, ambiguous, failure, cancellation, and replay states.

## Acceptance Criteria

Shared fixtures are deterministic and versioned; cross-cutting contracts have focused unit tests with exact expected values/errors; tests cover round trips, invalid schema, precedence/collision truth tables, absent-versus-present policy, marker topology, byte/text decisions, state transitions, authorized-delta classification, and status/diagnostic mapping without duplicating module-owned tests. Unit failures identify module, case ID, and fixture seed; no unit test depends on an unselected policy or a production global. Each shared row links to .74.1 and names any supporting implementation test owner.
design: Prefer small pure fixtures and table-driven assertions. Keep exact byte/text, delimiter, precedence, state, and diagnostic cases close to their owning module; defer process and filesystem effects to component tests.
acceptance_criteria: Each pure domain and parser module has focused unit tests with deterministic inputs and exact expected values/errors. Tests cover round trips, invalid schema, precedence/collision truth tables, absent-versus-present policy, marker topology, byte/text decisions, state-machine transitions, authorized-delta classification, and status/diagnostic mapping. Unit failures identify module, case ID, and fixture seed; no unit test depends on an unselected policy or a production global.
notes: Shared fixture and cross-domain unit owner. Feature leaves retain primary unit tests for their own parsing, sync, transaction, adapter, and lifecycle behavior; this bead supplies reusable fixtures and contracts.
close_reason: accepted after independent v3 review

title: Build executable clean-environment end-to-end script runner
description:
Build the executable clean-environment black-box runner mechanics. Create isolated HOME, source repositories, destination Git repositories and local remotes; select/build the packaged Omnirepo binary; invoke the same public commands a human or agent subprocess uses; capture exit status, stdout, stderr, durable records, Git refs, managed bytes/sections, and retained test artifacts. This bead owns process invocation, fixture-root lifecycle, case selection, and artifact collection, not the behavior journeys themselves. Journey definitions and assertions belong to .74.7; CLI status/stream mapping belongs to .31.5; low-level fixtures belong to .9.

## Acceptance Criteria

A runner can execute a named case from a clean checkout on each selected toolchain and leaves no state outside its temporary root. It exposes case selection, artifact roots, replay identity, and concise status while preserving detailed structured evidence. It uses no external network, credentials, installed agents, or ambient configuration. It fails on missing or extra expected effects supplied by the journey case and retains selected evidence for both success and failure.
design: The runner is the human/agent parity seam for the black-box suite. It should expose case selection, artifact roots, replay identity, and concise status while keeping all detailed evidence in structured bundles.
acceptance_criteria: A script can run from a clean checkout on each selected toolchain and leaves no state outside its temporary root. It exercises setup, first inferred sync, explicit policy, whole and partial content, source overlap, unchanged repeat, verification, commit/push, failure aggregation, cancellation, restart, repair, record-unavailable, and forbidden legacy paths. Each step has a stable case ID and the runner fails on missing or extra expected effects; successful and failed runs retain the decided evidence bundle.
notes: Public E2E runner mechanics only. .74.7 owns the complete journey matrix; .31.5 owns CLI process contract assertions; .9 owns fixture primitives.
close_reason: accepted after independent artifact-boundary, parallelism, failure-retention, host/MSRV execution, security, and autoreview proof; aggregate coverage gaps routed separately

title: Implement structured test event logging and evidence bundles
description:
Give unit, component, and E2E runners one versioned structured event stream. Emit step start/finish, case ID, suite, repository identity, stage, source/plan/config identity, attempt, seed, command classification, outcome, duration, artifact references, and sanitized diagnostics. Keep worker events out of direct terminal streams; aggregate them deterministically and apply the owner-selected evidence redaction, bounds, encoding, and retention rules before persistence or display.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Use typed events and one writer/aggregator for test evidence. Keep production run records and test bundles distinct, but share the selected identity, redaction, and bounded-output rules when their data crosses the same trust boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Every test step has a correlated start and terminal event, including skipped capability cases and harness failures. Logs remain parseable under parallel completion, preserve failure ordering and peer accounting, contain no secret/control-channel leakage, and point to the exact replay/artifact path. A failing assertion never suppresses fixture cleanup or later independent cases; terminal output is a concise projection of the structured bundle.
notes: Future self: logging is part of test correctness. A test that passes while losing its evidence or leaking a secret is not a passing test-system result.
close_reason: accepted after independent Rust 1.86, secret-scan, and autoreview verification

title: Add deterministic failure replay and diagnostic bundle tooling
description:
When a unit, component, or E2E case fails, write a bounded diagnostic bundle containing the test manifest version, case and fixture IDs, deterministic seed/barrier schedule, selected platform capabilities, sanitized command/config summary, event-log path, expected-versus-observed effect diff, and a one-command replay recipe. Support replay of process crashes, concurrent runs, interrupted journals, ambiguous Git delivery, repair attempts, and partial source availability without contacting real services.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Replay artifacts must be sufficient for a future agent to reproduce the failure without reading the entire implementation. Record the first failing assertion and all preceding durable events, while retaining peer outcomes and cleanup failures.
acceptance_criteria: Every failed required case is replayable or explicitly marked non-replayable with a typed reason. Replaying a saved seed reproduces the same assertion and event sequence within the selected platform contract; secrets and unbounded output are excluded; bundle creation failure is itself visible and cannot turn a failed suite green. Bundles distinguish harness failure, product failure, and unsupported capability.
notes: Future self: never serialize ambient credentials, absolute user secrets, or unbounded command output into a replay bundle.
close_reason: accepted after prior independent replay PASS and closure of corrected E2E runner prerequisite; aggregate coverage gaps routed separately

title: Make local and CI test execution failure-preserving
description:

title: Prove test isolation, anti-flake behavior, and cleanup
description:
Stress the composed test system rather than re-testing low-level fixture implementation. Exercise random case order, parallel workers, process leaks, late writers, crashed parents, interrupted artifact writes, colliding IDs, hostile filenames, symlink races, oversized output, platform capability skips, and repeated replay across the public unit/component/E2E runners. Repeated runs with the same seed and capability set produce equivalent results and structured evidence; unrelated cases cannot share HOME, ports, credentials, clocks, records, or Git state; leaked descendants and temp artifacts are detected; cleanup failures are reported without hiding the original failure.
