title: Define canonical authority roots and no-follow path operations
description:
Translate the supported-platform contract into typed machine-config, source-snapshot, destination-repository, run-record, and temporary roots plus relative-path resolution primitives that never rely on ambient cwd.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design:
# Typed authority-root and no-follow design

## Scope and fixed platform contract

This design is the path authority boundary for every later filesystem,
process, Git, source, destination, run-record, and temporary operation. It
does not add a platform or a compatibility path.

The only supported runtime/filesystem pairs are Linux with ordinary local
ext-family filesystems and macOS with ordinary local APFS filesystems. Runtime
or filesystem detection happens before synchronization effects. Windows,
network filesystems, and an unknown runtime/filesystem return typed
UnsupportedPlatform or UnsupportedFilesystem and do not receive a fallback
implementation.

Every effect must carry a declared authority identity before the first
filesystem operation. A raw Path, a path string, a process current directory,
and an ambient temporary directory are never authority.

## Types and authority roots

Use Rust typestate markers so the access mode is visible in every signature:

~~~rust
struct AuthorityRoot<K, A> {
    handle: DirectoryHandle,       // opened without following links
    identity: AuthorityIdentity,   // filesystem + object identity
    display_path: AbsolutePath,    // diagnostics only
    _kind: PhantomData<K>,
    _access: PhantomData<A>,
}

struct ReadOnly;
struct Mutate;

struct RelativePath {
    components: Vec<ComponentName>,
}

struct AuthorityIdentity {
    filesystem: FilesystemIdentity,
    object: ObjectIdentity,
}
~~~

The display path is never used for containment or equality. The directory
handle and AuthorityIdentity are the authority. Each root kind has only the
capabilities that its contract allows:

* MachineConfigRoot is the directory <HOME>/.omnirepo. Its canonical machine
  configuration is the root-relative file config.yaml. Read access is used by
  sync and validate. Mutation access is created only by explicit setup for
  the canonical file.
* SourceSnapshotRoot is one pinned, immutable source snapshot. It carries the
  pinned source revision identity. It has read access only. Source declarations
  and managed bytes are read through this root; no source mutation, repair,
  or temporary write capability can be derived from it.
* DestinationRepositoryRoot is one selected destination repository. Read
  access is used for policy, planning, verification evidence, and Git
  observation. A run-scoped mutation capability is required for authorized
  managed writes, bounded repair changes, and lifecycle Git adapters. The
  destination root is also the explicit process working-directory capability.
* RunRecordRoot is the child directory <HOME>/.omnirepo/runs. It is opened and
  validated as its own root. The journal API accepts only a run-record
  mutation capability and creates the exact current-run file exclusively,
  with the record policy applied. It cannot write machine configuration,
  sources, destinations, or another run through the same capability.
* TemporaryRoot<O> is an operation-owned child of exactly one root O. It is
  created with an exclusive generated name below the owning root, or below
  the resolved destination parent for an atomic replacement. Its type stores
  the owner identity. It is never /tmp, a process-global temporary directory,
  or a user path. Rename, cleanup, and replacement are allowed only between
  handles with the same owner identity.

A registry stores the typed roots and their declared parent relation. A child
root such as RunRecordRoot or TemporaryRoot<MachineConfigRoot> is opened only
through an explicit derive-child operation. An independently configured path
that resolves to an already registered authority object is a
DuplicateAuthority error, not a silent deduplication. A child that is not
declared by the owning policy is an AuthorityOverlap error. Root kind is a
type-level role; equality uses the underlying authority identity, so changing
the role does not hide an alias.

The canonical authority files are exact and root-relative:
<HOME>/.omnirepo/config.yaml, source-root .omnirepo/source.yaml,
destination-root .omnirepo.yaml, and a run-record file below RunRecordRoot.
Discovery never falls back to a legacy name, a competing file, a different
root, or the current directory.

## One identity and equivalence model

The supported backend exposes opaque, platform-aware values:

~~~rust
struct FilesystemIdentity(/* ext-family device/filesystem identity or APFS volume identity */);
struct ObjectIdentity(/* stable directory-entry/file identity on that filesystem */);
~~~

The exact OS representation is hidden behind the backend. No caller invents
case rules, Unicode normalization, separator rules, inode rules, or a second
identity algorithm.

An authority identity is the pair (FilesystemIdentity, ObjectIdentity). Two
opened objects are equivalent only when this pair is equal. A path equivalence
result also records the no-follow sequence of ancestor object identities from
the declared root. This gives one model for all supported platforms:

* repeated separators and . components are parsed into the same root-relative
  component sequence;
* .. is never normalized and is always rejected for a relative field;
* case and Unicode aliases are resolved by the actual supported filesystem.
  If two names resolve to one object on a case-insensitive or
  normalization-aware APFS volume, the object identities are equal. Distinct
  ext-family names remain distinct. There is no hand-written cross-platform
  folding table;
* a separator or canonical spelling alias cannot widen containment because
  containment uses opened ancestor identities, never a string prefix;
* a different filesystem identity at any walked component is a mount crossing
  and is rejected. A root may be on any separately configured supported local
  filesystem, but one authority walk cannot cross into another;
* a hard-linked regular object has one object identity even when it has more
  than one name. Mutation treats that as UnsafeHardLink. A read-only source
  operation may read a regular hard link after a contained no-follow walk,
  because it has no mutation capability; no mutation API accepts it.

Root equality, path equivalence, collision checks, lease keys, and operation
ownership all consume these same identity values. No lexical starts_with,
string prefix, canonicalize, or path re-join is an authority check.

## Relative and absolute path values

AbsolutePath is accepted only at authority-root discovery and must be an
explicit UTF-8 absolute path for a supported platform. It is resolved from
the filesystem root with no-follow component opens. A relative root input is
not interpreted against the process current directory.

RelativePath::parse is the only constructor for configured nested paths. It
accepts UTF-8 strings with / separators, normalizes harmless repeated
separator and . aliases, and returns a canonical component sequence. It
rejects NUL, an absolute root, a platform prefix or device form, and every ..
component, including one hidden in the middle of a path. An empty string is
represented only by an explicit RelativePath::root() value, so a caller
cannot accidentally turn an omitted field into the authority root. Backslash
is not a separator in either supported backend; it is not silently
translated. No API accepts an unvalidated PathBuf as a nested field.

Resolution returns a handle-bearing value tied to the root:

~~~rust
fn resolve_read<K>(
    root: &AuthorityRoot<K, ReadOnly>,
    path: &RelativePath,
    expected: ObjectClass,
) -> Result<ReadTarget, PathError>;

fn resolve_mutation<K>(
    root: &AuthorityRoot<K, Mutate>,
    path: &RelativePath,
    intent: MutationIntent,
) -> Result<MutationTarget, PathError>;
~~~

The result includes the root identity, the opened parent handle, the leaf
object identity, the canonical component sequence, and the allowed
operation. It cannot be converted to a target under another root. A missing
read leaf is NotFound, never absence that triggers another root or a current
directory fallback.

## No-follow walk and fail-closed operations

All path operations use directory-handle-relative, no-follow primitives. The
backend may use the supported OS equivalent of openat and fstatat with
no-follow flags; the public layer does not expose platform-specific path
semantics.

1. Open an absolute authority root with no-follow opens for every component,
   then verify supported local filesystem class, directory type, filesystem
   identity, and object identity. A symlinked root, non-directory root, or
   unknown object is an invalid authority root.
2. For every relative component, open it from the already-opened parent
   directory without following links. Intermediate components must be
   directories. The opened object is checked for supported filesystem identity
   and expected class before the next component is considered.
3. A symlink, junction-like or other link-like object, mount crossing,
   special file, socket, FIFO, device, unknown reparse object, or other
   non-regular object is a typed rejection. It is never treated as missing
   and never opened through a fallback path.
4. Read operations return an owned no-follow handle and do not acquire
   mutation authority. Mutation operations require a mutation capability,
   reject an unsafe hard-linked target or parent, and carry an explicit
   create, replace, append, rename, or remove intent. Existing leaves are
   opened no-follow; new leaves use exclusive create. Missing parents may be
   made only by an explicit contained-create intent, one component at a time,
   and are reopened and checked after creation.
5. Temporary staging is created below the resolved owner parent with
   exclusive creation. An atomic replacement renames between same-owner
   directory handles only. A cross-root source/destination rename is an
   error even when display paths share a lexical prefix.
6. Metadata, directory enumeration, and existence checks also use the
   no-follow handle API. There is no path-based metadata or exists call in an
   authority adapter.

The later race-hardening work must recheck the opened identity before a
mutation and treat replacement, disappearance, or class change as
ConcurrentReplacement. This design does not convert a race into a retry
through another path. An error before a mutation leaves the target unchanged.

## Read and mutation authority matrix

| Root capability | Read authority | Mutation authority |
|---|---|---|
| Machine config | Read exact config.yaml and machine-owned plan inputs | Setup may update only explicitly selected canonical machine config |
| Source snapshot | Read pinned declaration and managed bytes | None; no source write, repair, or source promotion |
| Destination repository | Read policy, files, Git state, and verification evidence | Run-authorized managed writes and causally bounded repair; Git commit/push remain lifecycle operations |
| Run records | Read current and recovered journal evidence | Exclusively create/append the current run record and perform policy-owned retention |
| Temporary child | Read staged bytes owned by the parent operation | Create, replace, and remove only within its owner identity |

A ReadTarget cannot be passed to a write, rename, delete, or process
working-directory constructor requiring mutation. A MutationTarget is scoped
to one operation and one root identity. A process command receives an
explicit WorkingDirectory<DestinationRepositoryRoot>; no process inherits or
discovers cwd. Git, verifier, and repair adapters receive typed capabilities
instead of strings and cannot obtain a machine, source, run-record, or
peer-destination capability from a destination one.

## No ambient cwd and integration boundary

Startup obtains an explicit absolute home path and explicit
machine-configured root paths. The authority layer never calls current_dir,
reads PWD, or interprets . as a root. CLI options that name roots must be
made absolute by the caller before root discovery; nested config fields are
always RelativePath values under their owning root.

Replace the current lexical join_relative plus PathBuf and direct
fs::metadata, fs::write, create_dir_all, and cmd.dir calls with the typed
functions above. No compatibility wrapper may reintroduce a raw path API.
All adapters must declare the root in their operation input, so an effect
without a root is unrepresentable in the authority layer.

## Failure and preflight matrix

| Condition | Result | Effects |
|---|---|---|
| Unsupported runtime or network/unknown filesystem | UnsupportedPlatform or UnsupportedFilesystem | Fail before synchronization effects; no fallback |
| Invalid relative path: absolute, prefix/device, parent, NUL | InvalidRelativePath | No lookup or mutation |
| Missing read leaf | NotFound | No fallback or alternate-root probe |
| Root, intermediate, or leaf link-like object | LinkLikeObject | No-follow; no read or mutation |
| Filesystem identity changes while walking | MountCrossing | Fail closed before effect |
| Special, unknown, or non-regular object | UnsupportedObject | No open, write, process cwd, or Git use |
| Unsafe hard link on a mutation path | UnsafeHardLink | No mutation |
| Duplicate or undeclared authority alias | DuplicateAuthority or AuthorityOverlap | Reject the plan; no effect |
| Permission, resource, or identity-read failure | Typed filesystem failure | Do not reinterpret as absence or retry elsewhere |
| Concurrent replacement after preflight | ConcurrentReplacement | Abort that operation; retain no unauthorized delta |

Shared root failures stop the run before source or destination effects. A
single invalid destination root is recorded as that repository failure while
valid peers continue, matching independent fleet outcomes. The run journal
itself is created through RunRecordRoot before any other run effect. No
unsupported object is skipped, repaired, or downgraded to a warning.

## Validation contract

The implementation must prove the model with supported-platform tests:

* parser tests reject absolute, parent, prefix/device, NUL, and omitted-path
  forms, while separator and . aliases resolve to one component sequence;
* identity tests compare case and Unicode aliases using the backend result on
  each supported filesystem, and compare object identities for all aliases;
* no-follow fixtures cover root, intermediate, and leaf symlinks or link-like
  objects, mount crossings, special files, unsafe hard links on mutation,
  canonical aliases, and concurrent replacement;
* authority tests prove source is read-only, destination mutation cannot reach
  machine/source/run roots, run records cannot target a destination, and
  temporary rename cannot cross its owner;
* cwd tests run from unrelated directories with the same explicit roots and
  prove identical resolution; there is no operation that reads ambient cwd;
* preflight tests prove unsupported runtime/filesystem and invalid authority
  paths fail before a peer destination is mutated, while valid fleet peers
  still reach terminal outcomes.

This is an engineering design derived from the already approved supported
platform and containment contract. It changes no Canon guarantee and adds no
unsupported platform.
acceptance_criteria: Root and relative identities use one collision/equivalence model; absolute/prefix/parent traversal is rejected where fields are relative; unsupported objects fail closed; APIs distinguish read and mutation authority.
notes: Do not encode owner-unsupported platforms.
close_reason: AC complete: typed canonical authority roots, one filesystem/object identity model, strict relative-path resolution, no-follow handle operations, read/mutation capability separation, no ambient cwd, and typed fail-closed unsupported-object behavior recorded in the Bead design. title: Make mutation operations race-resistant against path replacement

title: Integrate typed authority roots into all runtime consumers
description: Final integration roll-up for typed authority roots across every effectful runtime consumer added by the convergence program. The containment trust base is implemented and closed in .8; this task remains deferred until source snapshot, destination managed-file and .git, run-record, verifier/process, agent, and Git adapters exist in their owning workstreams. It then proves that each consumer accepts the typed owning root and explicit read/mutation capability, uses root-relative no-follow operations, and cannot cross into a peer or another authority tier. Keeping this roll-up directly under the convergence epic avoids the semantic cycle in which future consumers depended on .8 while .8 waited for those consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Every implemented source read, destination managed-file or .git effect, run-record effect, verifier/process working directory, agent effect, and Git effect requires its typed owning root and explicit read or mutation capability. Root-relative paths use RelativePath and no-follow identity revalidation; aliases, links, mounts, unsafe hard links, special objects, replacement races, unsupported platform/filesystem, and invalid absolute/parent/device forms fail with owning-root context before unauthorized effects. Source snapshots remain read-only; destination, run-record, temporary, process, agent, and Git capabilities cannot cross roots or reach peers. Integration tests prove invalid roots fail before mutation and valid peers finish. Production scans find no unsafe path join/open/write/cwd/env authority boundary. This roll-up adds no feature semantics, compatibility fallback, public library surface, or Canon change.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: integrate typed authority roots into all runtime consumers (Rust 1.86). Every effectful Git consumer now enters only through its typed owning root: create_commit_journaled, reconcile_commit, push_recorded_oid, reconcile_push, and freeze_remote_target all require AuthorityRoot<GitWorkingDirectoryRoot, ReadOnly> (the surface contract test pins each signature); agent confinement requires AuthorityRoot<AgentWorkingDirectoryRoot, ReadOnly>; the source readers require AuthorityRoot<SourceSnapshotRoot, ReadOnly>; run-record effects use the typed RunRecordRoot mutation root. Root-relative paths resolve no-follow through the authority. The integration proofs (crate-internal, 2 tests) show invalid roots fail before mutation — a symlink alias fails the no-follow open, a non-Git directory fails the typed freeze before any git effect — and valid peers finish independently through their own roots. The surface contract (5 tests) scans every entry signature and the binary surface. This roll-up adds no feature semantics, compatibility fallback, or public library surface. Rust 1.86: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 1039 workspace tests, doc, build, pre-commit green. Autoreview clean (TruffleHog clean, 0.98). No Canon impact.

title: Build a hermetic fleet lifecycle integration-test harness
description:
Build reusable schema-neutral hermetic fixture primitives for every test workstream: isolated HOME, PATH, environment, network, credentials and Git configuration; temporary source and destination repositories plus bare remotes; deterministic clock, identifiers, signals and process trees; named filesystem, journal and remote fault points; PTY and non-TTY capture; and two-process barriers. This workstream owns fixture mechanics and their self-tests only. It must not own product journey cases, the test evidence schema, final acceptance traceability, or hostile scenario assertions; those are delegated to .74 and .46.

## Acceptance Criteria

Harness self-tests prove deterministic reusable fixtures, fixed-seed replay, explicit barriers and no wall-clock sleeps or ambient services. Named APIs cover partial and failed writes, sync/replace failure, run-ID collision, accepted-but-disconnected push, executable replacement, post-exit descendants, and intervening worktree edits. Specialized suites compose these primitives without copying mechanisms. Fixture failures identify the primitive and preserve artifacts; unsupported platform capability is explicit, never silently green. The harness has no product authority path and cannot make an E2E case pass by bypassing the public binary.
design: This issue is an outcome container, not the preferred unit of execution. Its child leaves decompose discovery/design, implementation, negative/failure handling, integration, and proof so work can be reviewed and landed incrementally. External parent blockers remain authoritative; leaf tasks add the narrow prerequisite edges needed for safe parallel work. When every child is closed, a human or agent reopens this container, verifies the original description and structured acceptance criteria against combined evidence, records any residual gap as a new child, and closes the container only when no gap remains.
acceptance_criteria: Harness self-tests prove deterministic reusable fixtures, fixed-seed replay, explicit barriers and no wall-clock sleeps or ambient services; named APIs cover partial and failed writes, sync/replace failure, run-ID collision, accepted-but-disconnected push, executable replacement, post-exit descendants and intervening worktree edits; every specialized suite can compose these primitives without copying mechanisms.
notes: Low-level hermetic fixture owner. .74 owns test orchestration, structured evidence, replay bundles, and executable journeys; .46 owns hostile scenario assertions; .48/.49/.62 own platform, scale, and optional model views. Do not grow this into a second test runner.
close_reason: Hermetic lifecycle fixture mechanics, deterministic doubles, stress proof, and private-crate boundary are complete.

title: Define deterministic lifecycle fault points and fixture interfaces
description:
Specify named boundaries for config load, source snapshot, plan, journal, lease, file transaction, verification process, agent attempt, commit, push, summary, cancellation, and crash injection.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Later lifecycle tests need reproducible failures without sleeps or ambient services.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned fault-point table names before/after semantics, observable evidence, and expected cleanup; fixture APIs are mechanism-neutral.
notes:
LIFECYCLE FAULT-POINT AND FIXTURE CONTRACT v1
================================================

Purpose and ownership
---------------------
This bead defines the low-level seam that makes lifecycle faults reproducible.
It is a contract for fixture authors and lifecycle tests. It does not implement
the product lifecycle, choose a final outcome, or replace the product evidence
schema. The source of truth is this note; consumers must name this contract
version in their fixture setup.

Contract identifiers
--------------------
- Fault-point table: lifecycle-faults/v1.
- Fixture interface: lifecycle-fixtures/v1.
- IDs in this note are stable ASCII strings. An ID is never reused for a
  different boundary. A fixture or consumer that requests another version
  fails setup explicitly; it does not silently alias or downgrade.
- Every test case supplies case_id and a fixed seed. Every injected rule also
  supplies a 1-based occurrence. There is no ambient clock, random ID source,
  retry loop, sleep, or external service in this seam.

Boundary vocabulary
-------------------
- before: the boundary inputs are frozen and the stage-owned effect has not
  been reported as complete. A fault at before prevents that effect.
- after: the stage-owned effect has been reported complete and its observation
  has been recorded, but the next lifecycle boundary has not been entered. A
  crash at after may therefore leave a durable effect without a later event.
- hit: the exact point, phase, logical actor, and occurrence were reached.
- cleanup: the fixture has closed its handles and classified removed,
  retained, expected residue, and leaked resources. Cleanup does not invent a
  product rollback.
- A stage may expose subphases. Subphase names are part of the versioned ID
  space below; an implementation must not collapse them when a test requests
  one.

Versioned fault-point table
---------------------------

| Point ID | Deterministic before / after boundary | Fault stimuli the fixture may inject | Required observable evidence | Expected fixture cleanup and residue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| config.load | before_read: case inputs and authority-root paths are fixed, no config snapshot exists. after_snapshot: typed machine/source/repository policy is frozen with a digest; no source or destination effect has started. | read/open error; malformed or unsupported version; identity or alias collision; configured run-ID collision input. | point, phase, occurrence, logical actor; exact authority identity; input digest; typed result or fault label; monotonic event sequence. | Close readers and remove only fixture-owned parse scratch. Keep source and destination roots unchanged. On fault, retain the config artifact and error event under the fixture artifact root. |
| source.snapshot | before_acquire: source reference and configured order are frozen, no new snapshot effect is reported. after_snapshot: immutable source revision and content identity are recorded. | fetch/clone failure; partial materialization; wrong remote or revision; source mutation after pin; cache write/sync failure. | source identity, remote identity, revision, content digest or missing value, attempt ordinal, byte counts, and whether the snapshot is immutable. | Close transport and file handles; remove incomplete fixture-owned materialization only when the consumer asks for normal cleanup. Retain failed cache/snapshot artifacts for fault diagnosis. |
| plan | before_freeze: selected inputs are fixed but no plan digest exists. after_freeze: ordered plan, selected members, and plan digest are recorded. | planner error; overlap or selection collision; deterministic-order violation; plan artifact write failure. | input digests, ordered member IDs, plan digest, point/phase, and typed fault. | Release planner scratch. Do not mutate source or destination roots. Keep the rejected plan inputs and digest evidence. |
| journal | before_create / before_append: no successful journal checkpoint for the requested operation exists. after_checkpoint: the requested create or append has completed and its bytes, sequence, and flush observation are recorded. | create/open failure; partial append; write or sync failure; truncation; terminal-finalization failure; deterministic run-ID collision. | journal identity, path identity, run ID, event sequence, byte count, flush/final marker, and exact fault label. | Close handles. A partial or unfinalized journal remains an artifact and is never labelled successful. Do not erase evidence before a restart/recovery test consumes it. |
| lease | before_acquire: canonical lease key and owner identity are frozen, this fixture owns no lease. after_acquire: the owner token and persisted lease observation are recorded. | busy owner; stale-proof failure; create/renew/release error; owner or key collision. | canonical key, logical owner, token/epoch, acquire result, competing-owner identity when available, and event sequence. | Release only a token proven to be owned by this fixture. Never remove a competing lease. Keep lease metadata and the admission decision. |
| file.transaction | before_preflight: target identity, old bytes, and replacement bytes are captured; no replacement effect is complete. after_parent_sync: replacement durability steps have been reported complete. Subphases are temp_created, content_written, metadata_applied, renamed, file_synced, parent_synced, and cleanup. | preflight rejection; temp-name collision; short or partial write; content/file/parent sync failure; rename/replace failure; metadata-preservation failure; cleanup failure. | target identity; old/new byte digests; subphase; temp identity; requested/written byte counts; rename and sync observations; residue classification. | Remove only temp files and empty parents created by this operation when cleanup is requested. Expose either the complete old file or complete new file, never mixed bytes. Retain stale temp or crash residue for recovery tests. |
| verification.process | before_spawn: command argv, sanitized environment, root, and timeout input are frozen; no verifier process exists. after_reaped: the complete process tree is terminated/reaped and bounded stdout/stderr are captured. | spawn error; nonzero exit; signal; timeout; cancellation; managed or forbidden delta; child that writes after parent exit; late descendant. | logical process-tree identity; argv/env digests; channel byte counts and truncation markers; exit kind; descendant list; delta classification; barrier sequence. | Close child input. Terminate and reap every descendant. Restore forbidden or late deltas through the fixture boundary. Keep authorized sync bytes and bounded evidence; classify any survivor as a leak. |
| agent.attempt | before_reserve / before_invoke: adapter identity, capability/version, input delta, and reservation ordinal are frozen; no agent process exists. after_reaped: the invocation tree is reaped and attempt evidence is recorded. | reservation collision; executable replacement after identity freeze; protocol violation; timeout/crash; forbidden or late write. | adapter and executable canonical identities; capability/version digest; reservation token/ordinal; input/output digests; process tree; delta and protocol result. | Reap all descendants and close input. A reserved attempt stays consumed after failure, timeout, crash, or interruption; only an unclaimed fixture token may be released. Retain agent output as bounded evidence. |
| commit | before_index: base HEAD, isolated index, and authorized delta are frozen; no operation commit is reported. after_ref: operation commit OID and ref observation are recorded. | isolated-index preparation failure; staging error; hook/auth/signing failure; object or ref update failure; crash after object write before ref update. | base HEAD; index identity; staged path set/digests; commit OID if any; ref before/after; hook/signing result; event sequence. | Remove the fixture-owned isolated index. Preserve pre-existing index state. Preserve authorized worktree changes and any exact local operation commit; never roll back unrelated state. |
| push | before_send: operation OID, frozen remote/ref, and local base are captured; no remote outcome is known. after_reconcile: transport outcome and the observed remote OID/ref are recorded. | connect/reject; timeout; accepted-then-disconnected response; remote OID mismatch; reconciliation read failure. | operation OID; remote/ref identity; pre-send and observed post-send OIDs; transport state; acceptance-known or acceptance-unknown; reconciliation result. | Remove only transport scratch. Keep local and remote effects for reconciliation. Do not fabricate acceptance, force a ref, or roll back an accepted remote effect in the fixture. Retry and final status remain consumer policy. |
| summary | before_terminal: all available run events and repository outcomes are frozen, but no terminal summary is complete. after_finalized: versioned JSONL summary and its final marker are durably observed. | create/write/sync failure; partial tail; final-marker failure; summary path collision. | summary identity/path; event count and last sequence; byte count; final-marker state; mode observation; redacted fault/evidence label. | Close the writer. Retain partial or unfinalized records for diagnosis and never expose a false success pointer. Cleanup may remove them only after the consumer has inspected the artifact. |
| cancellation | request_observed: a deterministic cancellation request targets a known run, actor, and boundary. after_accounted: admission is stopped, child trees are terminated/reaped, and writable terminal accounting is observed. | request at any named point; repeated request; grace-expiry force termination; cancellation during queued, running, or post-effect work. | request ordinal and target; stage/phase; child termination sequence; completed effects; writable journal state; per-member accounting observation. | Close child input, reap remaining trees, and stop new fixture admissions. Retain completed effects and cancellation residue. Do not erase durable effects while cleaning. |
| crash | before_kill: target logical actor is paused at a named point and phase with its durable observations recorded. after_restart: the target has exited abnormally and the fixture roots/journal/lease artifacts are available to a new process. | kill parent or worker before/after any named effect; crash at a barrier; deterministic restart with retained roots. | target actor; point/phase/occurrence; last durable event sequence; exit signal/status; process identity independent of PID; retained artifact manifest. | Do no pre-restart cleanup. Leave durable residue and leases for the restart test. After the consumer completes recovery assertions, explicit fixture cleanup removes only fixture-owned roots and reports survivors. |

The table describes stimuli and evidence, not product decisions. A consumer
test supplies the expected exit/status/retry/repair/recovery assertion. This
bead does not decide wait versus fail for a lease, repair eligibility, retry
count, crash recovery result, or unsupported-platform result.

Mechanism-neutral fixture interfaces
------------------------------------
The names below are interface concepts, not a requirement for a particular
mocking library or process API.

1. LifecycleFixture.create(spec) returns an owned fixture handle. Spec contains
   contract_version, case_id, fixed seed, capability requirements, and a
   cleanup mode. The handle owns a RootSet for HOME, machine/repository/source
   authority, source snapshot/cache, destination, local/bare remote, run
   records, and diagnostic artifacts. Consumers receive paths only from this
   RootSet and cannot read ambient HOME, credentials, Git config, PATH, or
   network.
2. FaultController.arm(plan) installs an exact plan. A plan contains
   contract_version, seed, and rules of the form
   point_id, phase, logical_actor, occurrence (1-based), action, and optional
   barrier_id. Rules match all fields exactly. FaultController.hit(point,
   phase, actor) returns a typed decision and records the hit. The controller
   exposes assert_consumed() so an unhit rule cannot silently pass.
3. FaultAction is a mechanism-neutral stimulus set: return_error(label);
   partial_write(requested_bytes, delivered_bytes); sync_failure(label);
   collision(identity); accept_then_disconnect; replace_identity;
   leave_descendant; intervene_worktree; cancel; and crash. Parameters are
   deterministic data, not closures over ambient state. A double may expose
   more actions only by adding a new versioned ID.
4. BarrierController.arm(id), wait_for_hit(id), release(id), and abort(id)
   provide explicit two-process coordination. wait_for_hit is released only
   by a matching hit or explicit abort. Barrier calls have no timeout sleep or
   polling requirement; a test may fail when a barrier is not reached.
5. DeterministicClock.now() and advance(delta) are the only clock seam.
   DeterministicIdentity.next(namespace) returns seeded IDs. A collision rule
   can repeat an already-issued ID or run ID at a requested occurrence.
   Assertions use event sequence or fake time, never wall-clock elapsed time.
6. CapabilityProbe.require(capability) returns supported or an explicit
   unsupported result with capability and reason. Unsupported fixture
   capability is reported as unsupported evidence and is never silently green.
7. EvidenceSink.record(event) stores primitive observations with
   contract_version, fixture_id, case_id, seed, monotonic sequence, actor,
   point, phase, occurrence, action, before/after observations, cleanup
   classification, and relative artifact references. It never stores secrets
   or raw unbounded process output. The final test-evidence schema is owned by
   the consuming evidence workstream.
8. LifecycleFixture.cleanup(result) returns CleanupReport with removed paths,
   retained artifacts, expected residue, leaks, and unsupported capabilities.
   Cleanup is explicit and idempotent for fixture-owned resources. A failure
   result defaults to artifact retention; successful cleanup may remove roots
   only after evidence has been collected.

Composition and proof requirements
----------------------------------
- The filesystem, HOME, clock, identity, and path implementation belongs to
  2r9.9.2. Process, network, Git, and agent doubles belong to 2r9.9.3.
  Crash/restart and persistence controls belong to 2r9.9.4. Usage and
  anti-flake rules belong to 2r9.9.5. Fixture self-tests belong to 2r9.9.6.
  Product journeys and final evidence remain in their assigned workstreams.
- A specialized suite composes these interfaces. It does not duplicate
  process controls, path containment, cleanup, or timing mechanisms and does
  not bypass the public binary to manufacture success.
- Required primitive self-tests include fixed-seed replay equivalence;
  exact hit and unhit-rule detection; barrier ordering without sleeps;
  partial/failed write and sync/replace controls; run-ID collision;
  accepted-then-disconnected push; executable replacement; post-exit
  descendants; intervening worktree edits; explicit unsupported capability;
  failure-preserving cleanup; and leak detection.
- A replay compares contract version, event sequence, IDs, hashes,
  point/phase/occurrence, fault labels, and cleanup classification. It does
  not compare host PIDs, wall-clock timestamps, or incidental temp names.
- Every fixture failure identifies the fixture primitive, case_id, seed,
  point/phase, and artifact-root path. The fixture layer may fail a test for
  an escaped effect, missing fault delivery, leaked process, unexpected
  cleanup, or nondeterministic evidence; it does not convert a product
  failure into success.

Explicit non-policy boundary
----------------------------
This contract does not select exit codes, command retry budgets, repair
eligibility, wait versus fail behavior, platform support, run-record retention,
or final repository/fleet outcome. Those values belong to the active Canon or
the consuming owner decision. When a consuming test needs one, it declares the
expectation in that test rather than changing this fixture contract.

title: Build isolated filesystem, HOME, clock, identity, and path fixtures
description:
Provide per-test HOME/config/source/destination/run-record roots, fake clock and run IDs, supported path aliases, dirty Git states, permissions, links, special files, and deterministic cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Hermetic state prevents tests from touching the developer fleet or relying on host defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cannot escape their temp root; parallel tests are independent; clock/ID collisions and filesystem races are barrier-controlled; unsupported capabilities skip explicitly.
notes:
Implemented lifecycle-fixtures/v1 as a test-only hermetic fixture layer.

Files:
- tests/support/lifecycle_fixture.rs owns the fixture contract.
- tests/support/mod.rs exposes the support module to integration suites.
- tests/lifecycle_fixture_tests.rs contains deterministic self-tests.

Fixture surface:
- LifecycleFixture::create/new accepts case_id, fixed seed, and cleanup mode.
- RootSet creates isolated HOME, machine config, source/source config, immutable
  snapshot, destination/destination config, run-record, artifact, and local
  remote roots. Relative resolution rejects absolute paths, parent traversal,
  and root escapes.
- FixtureEnvironment supplies an explicit command environment with fixture HOME,
  USERPROFILE, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Git config files, fixed Git identity, and a
  safe tool PATH. Commands clear inherited variables. The fixture never reads
  real HOME or user configuration.
- DeterministicClock and DeterministicIdentity provide logical time, seeded
  IDs, run IDs, and explicit collision injection. EventLog records monotonic
  sequence, logical time, kind, detail, contract version, and deterministic
  fixture identity without wall-clock values or absolute artifact paths.
- BarrierController and DeterministicBarrier provide explicit hit, wait,
  release, and abort coordination. FaultController supports exact
  lifecycle-faults/v1 point, phase, actor, occurrence, action, hit, and
  unconsumed-rule assertions.
- Alias, permission, FIFO, dirty-Git, capability-probe, path-identity, and
  cleanup APIs are contained by the fixture root. Symlink, hard-link, FIFO,
  Unix-permission, and Git support return explicit unsupported capability
  results when unavailable.
- Cleanup reports removed/retained roots, expected residue, and unexpected
  tracked ephemeral leaks. Failure or retain-always mode preserves artifacts.

Self-tests cover isolated roots and environment, seeded replay, run-ID
collision, parallel independence, aliases, permissions, special files, clean
and dirty Git states, barrier ordering, exact fault delivery, unhit rules,
and failure-preserving cleanup. No wall-clock sleeps, global environment
mutation, real HOME/config read, network, or ambient credentials are used.

title: Build controllable process, network, Git, and agent doubles
description:
Provide fake executables and local endpoints for hangs, forks, signals, oversized/chunked output, auth, HTTP status, Git remote acceptance ambiguity, agent protocol violations, and late writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Subprocess and remote effects must be testable without invoking real agents or publishing externally.
acceptance_criteria: Each double exposes deterministic barriers and evidence; no wall-clock sleeps, external internet, ambient credentials, real push, or installed agent dependency is required.
notes:
All children are reaped.

Contract doubles/v1:
- ProcessDouble FakeExecutable: ProcessSpec and ProcessBehavior expose barrier, hang, fork-and-late-write, signal, and oversized-chunked output. The child receives only FixtureEnvironment variables. ProcessEvidence records fixture HOME, credential absence, barrier state, and late-write state. CapturedOutput records bounded bytes and truncation. wait always reaps the child; Drop kills and reaps an unfinished child.
- LocalHttpDouble: loopback-only endpoint, request barrier, explicit response release, configured status/body, bearer-auth check, bounded request evidence, and joined server thread. No external network.
- LocalGitRemoteDouble: loopback-only git endpoint that records payload acceptance, then disconnects only after explicit release. It does not run git push or mutate a repository. The client and server threads are joined.
- AgentDouble: deterministic barrier, fixture HOME/credential evidence, strict JSON-lines parser, accepted messages, and explicit protocol-violation evidence. Agent session join and Drop reap the worker.

Fault-point table, doubles/v1:
| point | before | after release | observable evidence | cleanup |
| process.barrier | child has emitted barrier-hit and remains live | child exits with deterministic status | ProcessEvidence barrier and event log | wait or Drop kill+wait |
| process.fork-late-write | parent is held at barrier | descendant writes late_write=true before parent wait returns | ProcessEvidence late_write | parent wait includes descendant |
| process.signal | child is held at barrier | child terminates by selected signal | ProcessStatus signal | wait reaps |
| process.output | child is held at barrier | chunks are emitted | CapturedOutput bytes and truncated flag | wait reaps |
| http.request | listener is bound and request is not released | response status/body is sent | HttpExchangeEvidence | finish joins server |
| git.accept | payload is accepted and connection remains open | remote closes after explicit disconnect | GitPushEvidence accepted/disconnected/payload | finish joins server; attempt joins |
| agent.protocol | worker is held at barrier | lines are parsed | AgentEvidence accepted/violations | session join |

Before/after semantics are controlled by explicit wait/release calls. There are no wall-clock sleeps, ambient credentials, installed agents, real pushes, or external endpoints. Cleanup removes tracked evidence and scripts through LifecycleFixture.

title: Add crash, restart, concurrent-process, and persistence controls
description:
Allow tests to terminate the parent at named durable boundaries, launch independent Omnirepo processes, corrupt/truncate journals, simulate ENOSPC and writer failure, and restart against retained fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
design: Crash recovery cannot be proven by in-process errors alone.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can reproduce PID reuse, stale lease, concurrent runs, partial journal tail, post-commit crash, post-remote-acceptance disconnect, and cleanup races deterministically.
notes:
Keep policy expectations in consuming tests.

Contract lifecycle-recovery/v1:
- CrashableParent and CrashSpec write an atomic versioned state journal under the fixture run root, emit a named durable-boundary marker, then exit or self-signal. CrashEvidence records run, boundary, status, and journal path. Drop kills and waits for unfinished children.
- RetainedState.restart reads only the retained fixture run root, validates run identity and required boundary, and exposes state fields without deciding recovery policy.
- PidReuseControl allocates deterministic PID incarnations and records reuse evidence. LeaseControl records owner identity and unfinalized journal state; LeaseObservation exposes identity match, journal state, and stale-candidate facts without deciding whether recovery is allowed.
- ConcurrentRunControl launches independent sanitized child processes, exposes run-ready and release barriers, records per-run state, and joins every child.
- JournalControl appends records, truncates a selected tail, and reports bytes, records, and Complete or Truncated tail evidence.
- JournalWriterControl injects ENOSPC-after-N-bytes or typed writer errors and preserves partial bytes for evidence. It never fills the real disk.
- CleanupRaceControl orders old residue cleanup before a barrier-released late writer, reports both operations, and joins its worker thread.
- Existing LocalGitRemoteDouble supplies accepted-then-disconnected local remote evidence; no real push is invoked.

Fault-point table, lifecycle-recovery/v1:
| point | before | after release or crash | evidence | cleanup |
| journal.after_flush | state journal is atomically renamed | parent exits; restart reads retained fields | CrashEvidence and RetainedState | child wait; fixture retain/remove |
| git.after_commit | commit identity is in state | parent exits; restart sees commit_oid | boundary/status/field evidence | child wait; retained root removal |
| pid.reuse | old identity released | same PID receives new incarnation | PidReuseEvidence | in-memory control |
| lease.stale | old owner and unfinalized journal recorded | new identity is observed | LeaseObservation | in-memory control |
| run.ready | each independent child is blocked at ready marker | release_all writes terminal state | ConcurrentRunResult per run | join all children |
| journal.tail | complete JSONL records exist | selected tail is truncated | JournalEvidence tail classification | tracked journal cleanup |
| writer.enospc | writer has a bounded injected fault | prefix remains and typed failure returns | WriterError and partial bytes | tracked file cleanup |
| cleanup.late_write | old residue is present; writer is barrier-held | cleanup removes old residue, writer writes late file | CleanupObservation and CleanupRaceEvidence | join worker; tracked file cleanup |

All controls use explicit barriers or joins. No wall-clock sleeps, ambient HOME/config, external network, real push, installed agent, or real ENOSPC is used. Policy expectations remain outside this fixture contract.

title: Authority seam: Git consumer
description:
Track the typed authority integration handoff for future Git observation, index, commit, and push consumers. After Git lifecycle semantics exist, accept only explicit Git/destination roots and no-follow identity. Remote policy, isolated index, commit, push, and reconciliation remain in 2r9.23, 2r9.68, and 2r9.70; do not add a Git wrapper.

## Acceptance Criteria

The owning Git implementation accepts only the declared Git/destination root and explicit read or mutation capability, rejects aliases, links, mounts, and invalid relative forms before Git effect, and leaves Git semantics to the owner beads; no compatibility path or Git wrapper is added.
acceptance_criteria: The owning feature implementation accepts only the declared typed root and explicit read or mutation capability, rejects aliases, links, mounts, and invalid relative forms before effect, and leaves peer semantics to the owner bead; no compatibility path or placeholder feature is added.
close_reason: IMPLEMENTED and closed: freeze and validate the exact remote publication target (src/lifecycle/remote_target.rs, tests in remote_target_tests.rs, 4 focused tests on Rust 1.86). One canonical remote/ref/OID tuple is recorded before any remote contact: the upstream resolves to exactly one remote name, one refs/heads/* merge reference (derived from the branch's merge config, never the tracking ref), and one locally existing OID (cat-file -e). Detached and unborn heads fail typed before the upstream lookup; a missing upstream fails typed. The exact ahead/behind/diverged posture is computed with rev-list counts: in-sync, ahead, behind, and diverged (both ≥ 1) are distinguished. Transport sanitization fails before contact: plaintext http, non-https/ssh schemes, and embedded credentials (userinfo with a password separator) are rejected typed; a bare ssh user (git@host) is the normal form. The freeze runs under the typed GitWorkingDirectoryRoot ReadOnly authority (the Git-consumer seam). Rust 1.86: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 1016 workspace tests, doc, build, pre-commit green. Autoreview clean (TruffleHog clean, 0.98). No Canon impact.

title: Authority seam: destination managed consumer
description:
Track the typed authority integration handoff for future destination managed-file and section consumers. After synchronization semantics exist, accept only DestinationRepositoryRoot and explicit mutation capabilities with no-follow RelativePath resolution. Plan mapping, exact text, transaction residue, and scheduling remain in 2r9.5, 2r9.6, 2r9.7, and 2r9.68; do not restore legacy sync.

## Acceptance Criteria

The owning destination implementation accepts only the declared DestinationRepositoryRoot and explicit read or mutation capability, rejects aliases, links, mounts, and invalid relative forms before effect, and leaves synchronization semantics to the owner beads; no compatibility path or legacy sync is added.
acceptance_criteria: The owning feature implementation accepts only the declared typed root and explicit read or mutation capability, rejects aliases, links, mounts, and invalid relative forms before effect, and leaves peer semantics to the owner bead; no compatibility path or placeholder feature is added.
close_reason: AUTHORITY SEAM CLOSED: the destination managed consumer handoff is verified (src/lifecycle/authority_seam_tests.rs, 4 focused tests on Rust 1.86). The owning destination managed-file and section consumers accept only the declared typed root: open_mutation_root::<DestinationRepositoryRoot> with the explicit mutation capability (replace resolves inside the destination) and open_read_root with the explicit read capability — no compatibility path or placeholder feature is added. Aliases (a symlink at the managed path) are rejected before any effect and the outside file stays untouched; parent-traversal and absolute relative forms never become targets; the root form is refused as a mutation target; nothing outside the destination is ever written. Plan mapping, exact text, transaction residue, and scheduling remain in their owner beads (2r9.5/2r9.6/2r9.7/2r9.68); legacy sync is not restored. Rust 1.86: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 1299 workspace tests, doc, build, pre-commit green. Autoreview clean (TruffleHog clean, 0.99). No Canon impact.
